extracted.intended_audience: CJR-X participants, hospitals (THs), organ procurement organizations (OPOs/IOPOs), histocompatibility laboratories (HCLs), and other stakeholders subject to CMS Innovation Center model and Medicare reimbursement rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and proposed policies for CJR-X participants (including attestation, clinician/financial reporting, and standard provisions) and proposed revisions to IOPO/HCL organ acquisition reimbursement and reconciliation rules. Focuses on required attestations, quarterly lists, cost reporting, interim rates, and reconciliation procedures under Medicare regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEHRT use attestation for AAPM option
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X participants who wish to participate in the AAPM option must attest to meeting the CEHRT use requirement that meets the CEHRT definition in our regulations at 42 CFR 414.1305 on an annual basis prior to the start of each performance year in a form and manner and by a date specified by CMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attestation is voluntary; CJR-X participants who choose not to attest are assigned to the non-AAPM option. Participants must retain and provide CMS access to the attestation upon request. Participants choosing AAPM must also provide their CMS EHR Certification IDs on an annual basis prior to the end of each performance year in a form and manner and by a date specified by CMS. CMS notes attestation may affect clinicians' ability to qualify as QPs (clinicians of participants who do not attest would not be assessed for QP status).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of AAPM option vs non-AAPM option
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed definitions for the 'AAPM option' and 'non-AAPM option' at §512.605, and CMS assignment of CJR-X participants to AAPM or non-AAPM based on CEHRT attestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS seeks comment on these definitions and assignment approach. The decision to attest or not to attest has downstream implications for clinicians' QP determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial arrangements list submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each CJR-X participant must submit information about the eligible clinicians or MIPS eligible clinicians who enter into financial arrangements with the CJR-X participant for purposes of supporting the CJR-X participant's cost or quality goals (the 'financial arrangements list').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission is required in a form and manner and by the date specified by CMS on a quarterly basis during each performance year or the participant may attest that there are no individuals to report. The financial arrangements list is proposed to satisfy the criteria to be considered an Affiliated Practitioner List (42 CFR 414.1305). The list will be used for QP determinations and APP reporting, and must be retained and provided to CMS upon request. CMS seeks comment on content, periodicity, and submission method to minimize burden while ensuring sufficient information for QP and APP processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must be listed on the financial arrangements list
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of CJR-X, the eligible clinicians or MIPS eligible clinicians to be reported include: (1) CJR-X collaborators engaged in sharing arrangements with a CJR-X participant; (2) PGP, NPPGP, or TGP members who are collaboration agents engaged in distribution arrangements with a PGP/NPPGP/TGP that is a CJR-X collaborator; and (3) PGP/NPPGP/TGP members who are downstream collaboration agents engaged in downstream distribution arrangements with a PGP/NPPGP/TGP that is also an ACO participant in an ACO that is a CJR-X collaborator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will use the submitted list to make determinations regarding which physicians and nonphysician practitioners should receive QP determinations or be reported for the APP based on services furnished under CJR-X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required data elements for CJR-X collaborator entries
rubrics_metrics.description: For each CJR-X collaborator who is a physician, nonphysician practitioner, or therapist during the performance year, the financial arrangements list must include the name, tax identification number (TIN), and national provider identifier (NPI) of the CJR-X collaborator; and the start date and, if applicable, end date, for the sharing arrangement between the CJR-X participant and the CJR-X collaborator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data must be provided in the form and manner and by the date specified by CMS; participants must retain the list and provide CMS access on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required data elements for collaboration agent entries
rubrics_metrics.description: For each collaboration agent who is a physician, nonphysician practitioner, or therapist during the performance year, the financial arrangements list must include the name, TIN, and NPI of the collaboration agent and the name and TIN of the CJR-X collaborator with which the collaboration agent has entered into a distribution arrangement; and the start date and, if applicable, end date, for the distribution arrangement between the CJR-X collaborator and the collaboration agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission, retention, and CMS access requirements apply; quarterly reporting or attestation of none-to-report is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required data elements for downstream collaboration agent entries
rubrics_metrics.description: For each downstream collaboration agent who is a physician, nonphysician practitioner, or therapist during the performance year, the financial arrangements list must include the name, TIN, and NPI of the downstream collaboration agent and the name and TIN of the collaboration agent; and the start date and, if applicable, end date, for the downstream distribution arrangement between the collaboration agent and the downstream collaboration agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly submission or attestation of none-to-report; retention and provision to CMS upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinician engagement list submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X participants must submit a clinician engagement list on a quarterly basis during each performance year (or attest there are no individuals to report) that lists eligible clinicians or MIPS eligible clinicians who participate in CJR-X activities, have a contractual relationship with the CJR-X participant, and who are not listed on the financial arrangements list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will use the clinician engagement list to assess QP determinations and for APP reporting. Submission is intended to align with Quality Payment Program's QP determination dates (42 CFR 414.1425). Participants must retain and provide CMS access to the list upon request. CMS recognizes this may create administrative burden but expects benefits in terms of correct QP determinations and MIPS APM scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required data elements for clinician engagement list
rubrics_metrics.description: For each physician, nonphysician practitioner, or therapist not listed on the financial arrangements list but who has a contractual relationship with the CJR-X participant and participates in CJR-X activities during the performance year, the clinician engagement list must include the name, TIN, and NPI of the clinician; and the start date and, if applicable, end date, for the contractual relationship between the clinician and the CJR-X participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly reporting or attestation of none-to-report; retention and CMS access requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly periodicity and attestation option
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of the financial arrangements list and clinician engagement list is proposed on a quarterly basis during each performance year or the CJR-X participant may attest that there are no individuals to report on each list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly timing is proposed to align with QP determination dates (42 CFR 414.1425). CMS seeks comment on the periodicity and methods of submission to minimize reporting burden while providing sufficient information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and CMS access for submitted documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X participants would be required to retain and provide CMS access to the financial arrangements list, clinician engagement list, and CEHRT attestations upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention requirements are essential for CMS determinations; failure to retain/provide upon request could affect compliance and QP/APP processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Standard Provisions for Innovation Center Models
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X meets the criteria for application of the Standard Provisions for Mandatory Innovation Center Models (42 CFR part 512, subpart A). Unless otherwise specified, all CJR-X participants and CJR-X beneficiaries would be subject to the provisions at §§512.100 through 512.190.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standard provisions address Beneficiary Protections; Cooperation in Model Evaluation and Monitoring; Audits and Record Retention; Rights in Data and Intellectual Property; Monitoring and Compliance; Remedial Action; Innovation Center Model Termination by CMS; Limitations on Review; Miscellaneous Provisions on Bankruptcy and Other Notifications; and Reconsideration Review Process. CMS seeks comment on whether CJR-X should include model-specific provisions related to any of these areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination provisions for CJR-X
rubrics_metrics.description: The general provisions relating to termination of the model by CMS in §512.165 would apply to CJR-X. In the event CMS terminates CJR-X, CMS would provide written notice to participants specifying the grounds and effective date of termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As provided by section 1115A(d)(2) of the Act, termination of the model under section 1115A(b)(3)(B) would not be subject to administrative or judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: IOPO/HCL reasonable cost reimbursement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed to hold independent organ procurement organizations (IOPOs) and histocompatibility laboratories (HCLs) to reasonable cost reimbursement for organ acquisition and transplantation services in accordance with section 1861(v) of the Act; revise §413.420 to change 'kidney' to 'organ' and apply reasonable cost principles to non-renal organs for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes revising regulatory text across §413.420 (multiple subsections), and is intended to ensure costs are reasonable, necessary, related to patient care, reconciled to payments made by THs and OPOs, and to prevent inflated charges and profits from organ procurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: IOPO/HCL agreement requirements with CMS (§413.420(c) obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any IOPO or HCL that wishes to have the cost of its pre-transplant services reimbursed under Medicare must file an agreement with CMS under which the IOPO or HCL agrees to: (1) file a cost report in accordance with §413.24(f) within 5 months following the close of the period covered by the report; (2) permit CMS to designate a contractor to determine interim reimbursement rates and to determine Medicare's reasonable cost based upon the cost report filed by the IOPO or HCL; (3) provide budget or cost projection information as required to establish an initial interim reimbursement rate; (4) pay to CMS amounts that have been paid by CMS to THs and that are determined to be in excess of the reasonable cost of services provided; and (5) not to charge any individual for items or services for which that individual is entitled to have payment made under section 1881 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These agreement provisions are proposed to apply to both kidney and non-renal organs once §413.420's scope is revised; CMS proposes rephrasing to reflect accrual accounting (payments 'have been received or are receivable').

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor establishment and publication of non-renal interim rates (non-renal SACs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the Medicare contractor to establish (and adjust if necessary) non-renal organ-specific Standard Acquisition Charges (SACs) or contractor established rates for IOPOs and HCLs, and to disseminate these interim rates to all transplant hospitals (THs), OPOs, and contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adequate cost data is not available to determine initial interim rates, the contractor would determine them based on the IOPO's or HCL's estimate of projected costs for the fiscal year. This mirrors procedures used for kidney SACs and aims to increase transparency, ensure reasonable cost compliance, and prepare for reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim rate payment reconciliation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments made by THs and OPOs on the basis of interim rates are to be reconciled directly with the IOPO or HCL after the close of its fiscal year in accordance with §413.420(e); for non-renal organs, this applies for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconciliation implements reasonable cost determinations and retroactive adjustments in accordance with the accrual basis of accounting (see §413.24(a) and §413.64(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of OPOs as payors for interim rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise §413.420(a)(2) and related provisions to include OPOs as entities that pay IOPOs and HCLs for pre-transplantation services based on interim rates established by the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes that OPOs also pay IOPOs and HCLs and ensures they receive interim rate information; conforming changes proposed across §413.420 subsections to add OPOs where payors are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on profiting from organ procurement and non-profit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: OPOs are required to operate as non-profit organizations under Federal regulations and to only recover their reasonable costs associated with organ procurement activities; they cannot profit from the organs themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS emphasizes the fundamental principle that human organs are donated gifts, not commodities for sale. Oversight and reconciliation proposals are aimed at enforcing this principle and correcting inflated charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: IOPO/HCL organ-specific acquisition charge methodology (per §413.404(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each non-renal organ type, an IOPO is supposed to establish its organ-specific non-renal acquisition charges by estimating the reasonable and necessary organ acquisition costs it expects to incur, divided by the projected number of organs it expects to procure in its cost reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MACs can use cost report data to determine if established acquisition charges are higher than reasonable costs actually incurred; inflated charges billed to THs become organ acquisition costs reported on TH cost reports and may lead to Medicare sharing in inflated costs. Proposed contractor review and reconciliation seeks to prevent this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation delay and updates to cost reporting form
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed delay in implementation for non-renal organ reimbursement policy to allow time to update the IOPO and HCL cost reporting form CMS-216-94 (OMB control number 0938-0102) and allow IOPOs and HCLs time to prepare for changes. The non-renal reasonable cost reimbursement applies for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explicitly links the implementation timeline to necessary form updates and stakeholder readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accrual-basis accounting reflection in payment adjustment language
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rephrasing in §413.420(c)(1)(iv) and related sections to use language reflecting the accrual basis of accounting required at §413.24(a), e.g., specifying IOPO or HCL agrees to pay CMS amounts that 'have been received or are receivable' and specifying retroactive adjustments in accordance with §413.64(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change is to ensure consistency with accounting rules and proper treatment of receivable payments during reconciliation and retroactive adjustments.
